ghidra: read-only: no rename, comment, prototype, function creation or save
subject: Why FLAK (category 5), DEPTHCHARGE (category 8) and CATAPULT (category 0Bh) take exactly zero assignments on IJN01, established separately for each.
reuses: include/bsp/gunnery_tables.hpp (kGunneryPreferenceLists, build_rank_table_00727bd0, gunnery_rank), include/bsp/unit_gunnery_pass.hpp (kArtilleryCategories, kAaFlakCategories, kTorpedoCategories, kDepthChargeCategories, kCategoryMaskMayEngagePlane/Other, WeaponGroup), include/bsp/bullet_engagement_range.hpp. No new header or source was published.

verdicts.depthcharge_cat8: faithful zero. Not a defect. The gunnery pass does assign category 8 like any other gun category; it is refused by the engagement range, 970 m to the nearest submarine against a 240 m category range. In the native build 00862820's category-8 arm refuses independently whenever the submarine is shallow, so the zero holds whichever way the depth resolves.
verdicts.flak_cat5: faithful zero, and a consequence of the aircraft never flying. Two independent sufficient causes: (a) the authored row ranks 8 aircraft classes and MTorpedoBoat, and side 1 on IJN01 has no MTorpedoBoat and nothing else the row ranks within reach - the 1938 m candidate at California is No19, a submarine the flak row does not rank; (b) no aircraft comes within 2960 m of any unit, against an isolated category-5 range of 2000 m on Enterprise and a game-wide flak ceiling of 2400 m.
verdicts.catapult_cat0b: faithful zero, structural. The row at 00E0A374 is zero in all 61h dwords, so gunnery_rank(0Bh, *) is 0 for every class id and every candidate is refused on the first test. All 20 CATAPULT device records in the installation author no Bullet key at all, against 402 of 402 for every other Function: a catapult is an aircraft launch device, not a weapon, and the gunnery pass should never assign it.

routines.name: the rank table producer, 00E092C8 -> 00E19BF8
routines.note: rank[category*61h + classId] is the one-based position among the non-zero entries. A zero entry is SKIPPED (JZ 00727BF7 -> 00727C05, the pointer advance), not a terminator; the inner loop always runs 61h times (ESI = EDX + 60h at 00727BF0). Category 0's id 61h writes to 00E19BF8+184h, the first dword of rank row 1, which row 1's own REP STOSD at 00727BEC erases. No other row holds an id above 46h, so no other rank row is touched and row 0Bh is genuinely all zero.

routines.name: BSP_UnitGunneryAi_TargetClassAllowed, the class gate
routines.note: Args confirmed from the frame and the RET 8: [ESP+8] category (EDI), [ESP+0Ch] target (ESI). Four liveness bytes at 00862825; the per-(category,class) permission byte [this + cat*61h + classId + 0CCh] at 00862855; the rank at 0086285F; the category-7 arm at 00862869; the submarine arm at 0086288C - categories 8 and 9 refuse a shallow submarine, every other category except 7 refuses one that is not shallow, and category 7 is exempt from both.

routines.name: BSP_Entity_IsAboveDepthChargeDepth
routines.note: returns [sub+100h] > ([sub+1204h] + [sub+1200h]) / 3.0, with 3.0 the double at 00D7A2B0. Direction established from its two siblings' consumers rather than from the existing name.

routines.name: the submarine deck-gun depth predicate
routines.note: returns [sub+100h] > [sub+1200h] - 3.0. 008627A0, the class-8 category gate, lets a submarine's own categories 1, 2, 5 and 6 run only when this holds.

routines.name: the submarine torpedo depth predicate
routines.note: returns [sub+100h] > [sub+1204h] - 3.0, the periscope reference. 008627A0 gates the submarine's own category 7 on it.

routines.name: BSP_UnitGunneryAi_SetArtilleryGroupAllowed
routines.note: walks 00E0A4F8 = {1, 2, 3, 4, 6} terminated by 0Ch, and ORs 2 or ANDs ~2 into mask[cat] at this+80h+cat*4 - the non-plane bit. docs/DIRECTOR_UPDATE_ARMS.md's coverage table calls it unread; that entry is stale, the ledger record from cc2_unit_gunnery_pass already carried the list and the bit operation.

routines.name: BSP_UnitGunneryAi_SetAaGroupAllowed
routines.note: walks 00E0A510 = {1, 5, 6}, ORs 1 or ANDs ~1 - the plane bit. Category 5's mask is therefore 3 whether aaEnabled is set or clear, because the constructor already seeded 3 and this setter only touches bit 0. docs/DIRECTOR_UPDATE_ARMS.md's coverage table calls it unread; that entry is stale, the ledger record from cc2_unit_gunnery_pass already carried the list and the bit operation.

routines.name: BSP_UnitGunneryAi_SetTorpedoGroupAllowed
routines.note: walks 00E0A520 = {7}; writes the whole word 3 or 0 and mirrors the flag to this+77h. docs/DIRECTOR_UPDATE_ARMS.md's coverage table calls it unread; that entry is stale, the ledger record from cc2_unit_gunnery_pass already carried the list and the bit operation.

routines.name: BSP_UnitGunneryAi_SetDepthChargeGroupAllowed
routines.note: walks 00E0A528 = {8, 9}; writes the whole word 3 or 0 over mask[8] and mask[9] and mirrors the flag to this+78h. docs/DIRECTOR_UPDATE_ARMS.md's coverage table calls it unread; that entry is stale, the ledger record from cc2_unit_gunnery_pass already carried the list and the bit operation. Alone among the four it has no refreshAll bypass at its call site (008625D9 compares director+223h against bridge+10h with no preceding TEST BL,BL), so it fires only on a change - and the bridge's first call is always a change because 00863AD1-00863ADD zero bridge+0Ch..+10h while director+223h defaults to 1 at 007202FD.

corrections.was: Categories 1, 5, 8 and 11 ... list plane classes, air classes, the submarine and nothing at all. No plane and no submarine exists on this mission, so 00862820 step 3 refuses every candidate on a zero rank. That is the table doing its job.
corrections.is: That measurement was a different mission. On IJN01 two submarines do exist, are visible, and are engaged by categories 4 and 6 - the run's per-gun table names No19 as the target of nine category-4 guns. Category 8's row ranks MSubmarine FIRST, so its zero is not a zero rank; it is the 240 m engagement range against 970 m. The zero-rank explanation stands only for category 11.

corrections.was: 00862820 requires it before letting the depth-charge categories 8 and 9 take a target answering IsKindOf(8).
corrections.is: Inverted. 008628AE JZ 008628C7 sends a ZERO answer to the MOV AL,1 return and falls a non-zero answer through to 008628B0 XOR AL,AL / RET 8. Categories 8 and 9 require 00852820 to be FALSE - a depth charge engages a submarine only when it is NOT above depth-charge depth. The opposite arm at 008628B7 exempts category 7 and, for every other category, refuses at 008628C5 when the answer is zero. The two arms are complementary.

divergence.what: score_candidate_00863990 calls bsp::target_is_engageable_00862820(liveness), which carries only the four liveness bytes. 00862820's category-7 arm, its submarine arm and its [this + cat*61h + classId + 0CCh] permission byte are all absent, so the host is strictly more permissive than the native gate.
divergence.effect_on_this_measurement: none. Category 8's zero on IJN01 comes from the range gate, which the host does implement, and the missing arm would only have refused it harder. The divergence is already recorded as a correction by docs/TORPEDO_CATEGORY_ADMISSION.md section 7; this packet confirms it from the listing and supplies the sign convention for 00852820.
divergence.prescription: 1. Add a bool target_is_shallow_00852820(std::size_t unit) query to the unit binding, answering [sub+100h] > ([sub+1204h] + [sub+1200h]) / 3.0f from PeriscopeDepth / SwimDepth2 and the unit's vertical coordinate; a unit that is not IsKindOf(8) never reaches it. 2. In score_candidate_00863990, after the liveness test and before the rank test, refuse when category is 8 or 9 and the query is true, and when category is neither 7 nor 8 nor 9 and the query is false. 3. Add the category-7 arm at the same point: require IsKindOf(6), reject IsKindOf(0Eh). 4. Add the [this + cat*61h + classId + 0CCh] permission array as all 1, or record it as deliberately omitted because no mission script in this installation writes it. The integrator owns the host; this packet publishes no source.

assumptions: The 240 m category-8 range on Cassin is DERIVED, not observed: from 006E9890's depth-charge arm, from Mahan 1941 (VehicleClass[309], the run's own type_id line for Cassin) carrying device class 54 'US Destroyer DC launcher' with bullet class 54, and from that bullet's Type = 'Depthcharge' with no FlyTime. The run prints no per-category range, and 240 is below Cassin's best_range of 1500, so it cannot be read off the log; Enterprise's 2000 for category 5 IS read off the log, because Enterprise carries no category with a longer range. The Mona and PT vehicle classes were not looked up, so their category-8 bullet class is assumed to be one of the four real depth-charge classes - all four give 240 and all five units are over 3.2 km from anything, so no verdict turns on it. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether No18 and No19 are above or below the depth-charge threshold on IJN01 - the host models no submarine depth, ForceSubmarinePeriscope is commented out in every mission script in the installation and ijn_1_pearl.lua never calls it, so the depth-charge verdict was written to hold either way but the reason the native build refuses is not settled. NOT ESTABLISHED: the absolute sign of [sub+100h], [sub+1200h] and [sub+1204h]; XMM1's producer in 00853630's copy loop was not chased. The relative reading - three routines comparing one coordinate against a surfaced, a periscope and an averaged reference - is complete and is what the verdicts use.
